111	    def all_to_all_4d(
112	        self,
113	        x: torch.Tensor,
114	        *,
115	        mode: int = 0,
116	        out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
117	        seq_splits: list[int] | None = None,
118	        head_splits: list[int] | None = None,
119	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
120	        """mode 0 scatters heads and gathers sequence; mode 1 inverts it.
121	
122	        Returns a tensor the caller owns, with no lifetime rules. ``out`` from ``empty_output()``
123	        skips the copy-out; any other contiguous CUDA tensor of the output shape is copied into.
124	
125	        ``seq_splits[p]`` / ``head_splits[p]`` are rank p's sequence and head shard: pass both or
126	        neither, identical on every rank and matching the shape handed in. Neither means even
127	        shards. Collective: every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes.
128	        """
129	        if out is None:
130	            return torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d(
131	                self._handle, x, mode, seq_splits, head_splits
132	            )
133	        # Refused rather than silently wrong, for the same reason the async call refuses: the
134	        # out-variant mutates a buffer the caller already owns, so it carries no autograd formula
135	        # and what comes back is that buffer -- backward() would run to completion and leave
136	        # x.grad as None. The returned value cannot signal it either, since nothing distinguishes
137	        # a caller who wanted no gradient from one whose gradient was dropped.
138	        if torch.is_grad_enabled() and x.requires_grad:
139	            raise RuntimeError(
140	                "all_to_all_4d(out=...) does not support autograd: the out-variant is a mutating "
141	                "op with no backward, so the gradient would be dropped without an error. Drop "
142	                "out=, or run under torch.no_grad()."
143	            )
144	        # Two ops, one method: the out-variant declares the alias it really has, which is what
145	        # keeps the functional one differentiable. See the note in src/bindings.cc.
146	        torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d_out(
147	            self._handle, x, mode, seq_splits, head_splits, out
148	        )
149	        return out

151	    def all_to_all_4d_async(
152	        self,
153	        x: torch.Tensor,
154	        *,
155	        mode: int = 0,
156	        out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
157	        seq_splits: list[int] | None = None,
158	        head_splits: list[int] | None = None,
159	        lend: bool = False,
160	    ) -> torch.Tensor | CompletedHandle:
161	        """``all_to_all_4d`` on this group's comm stream, returning immediately.
162	
163	        The result is an ``AsyncCollectiveTensor``: ``.wait()`` returns the plain tensor, and so
164	        does the first use by any aten op -- either way the caller's stream waits on the comm
165	        stream's completion event GPU-side, and the host does not block. A view op re-wraps without
166	        waiting.
167	
168	        ``lend=True`` gets ``out=``'s saving without a buffer of your own: the peers write a window
169	        this group holds, the result IS that window, and there is no copy-out. The group rotates
170	        through four windows per dtype, so at most four lent results may be alive at once -- a
171	        fifth call raises rather than overwriting one, and the count is per rank, so every rank has
172	        to drop its results at the same point in its own program. Mutually exclusive with ``out=``.
173	        Like the rest of this method it is not differentiable.
174	
175	        Wait on, or use, every result: a dropped one leaves its entry in torch's work registry, and
176	        ``out=`` is the hole, since reading your own ``out`` never touches the registry. On a
177	        libtorch with no ``c10d::register_work`` this returns a ``CompletedHandle`` instead --
178	        correct, no overlap, and a distinct type so it is visible.
179	        """
180	        # Refused rather than silently ignored: both ask for the zero-copy path, and picking one
181	        # for the caller would leave a lend=True that quietly did nothing.
182	        if out is not None and lend:
183	            raise ValueError(
184	                "all_to_all_4d_async takes out= or lend=True, not both: each is a way of getting "
185	                "the zero-copy path, one with a buffer you own and one with a window the group "
186	                "lends. Drop whichever you did not mean."
187	            )
188	        # Refused rather than silently wrong. AsyncCollectiveTensor is built with
189	        # _make_wrapper_subclass(..., requires_grad=elem.requires_grad), which makes the wrapper a
190	        # LEAF: autograd runs above the subclass and never sees the wrapped tensor's history, so
191	        # backward() would deposit the gradient on the wrapper and leave x.grad as None.
192	        if torch.is_grad_enabled() and x.requires_grad:
193	            raise RuntimeError(
194	                "all_to_all_4d_async does not support autograd: its result is an "
195	                "AsyncCollectiveTensor, which is a leaf, so the gradient would be dropped without "
196	                "an error. Use all_to_all_4d()."
197	            )
198	        # This group's device, not the current one: an aten op on `x` runs on the current stream
199	        # of x's device whatever device is current, and that stream is what the transfer has to be
200	        # ordered against. With another device current, the no-argument form names a stream on it,
201	        # which orders nothing here and cannot take record_stream() for this tensor.
202	        caller = torch.cuda.current_stream(self.device)
203	        with torch.cuda.stream(self._comm_stream):
204	            if out is None:
205	                y = torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d_staged(
206	                    self._handle,
207	                    x,
208	                    mode,
209	                    seq_splits,
210	                    head_splits,
211	                    caller.stream_id,
212	                    caller.device_index,
213	                    lend,
214	                )
215	            else:
216	                torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d_staged_out(
217	                    self._handle,
218	                    x,
219	                    mode,
220	                    seq_splits,
221	                    head_splits,
222	                    out,
223	                    caller.stream_id,
224	                    caller.device_index,
225	                )
226	                y = out
227	        registered = _C.register_stream_completion(y, self._comm_stream.cuda_stream)
228	        # Two streams touch the output: one allocated it, the other wrote it, and the caching
229	        # allocator must know about the cross-stream use before it may recycle the block.
230	        y.record_stream(self._comm_stream)
231	        y.record_stream(caller)
232	        return AsyncCollectiveTensor(y) if registered else CompletedHandle(y)
233	
234	    def empty_output(
235	        self,
236	        x: torch.Tensor,
237	        *,
238	        mode: int = 0,
239	        seq_splits: list[int] | None = None,
240	        head_splits: list[int] | None = None,
241	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
242	        """A buffer shaped like ``all_to_all_4d(x, mode=...)``'s output, in symmetric memory.
243	
244	        Passing it back as ``out=`` makes the peers write it directly, which removes the copy-out.
245	        You own it: keep it across steps, free it when you like, and it may outlive the group.
246	        COLLECTIVE, so allocate outside the loop -- and use one buffer per concurrent call, since a
247	        call overwrites it.
248	        """
249	        return torch.ops.fast_ulysses.empty_output(self._handle, x, mode, seq_splits, head_splits)
250	
251	    def _timed(
252	        self,
253	        x: torch.Tensor,
254	        *,
255	        mode: int = 0,
256	        seq_splits: list[int] | None = None,
257	        head_splits: list[int] | None = None,
258	    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, float]]:
259	        """BENCHMARKS ONLY: the copying call with CUDA events between its stages, which sum to the
260	        whole call because they are strictly ordered on one stream. Reading the events syncs."""
261	        out, stages = torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d_timed(
262	            self._handle, x, mode, seq_splits, head_splits
263	        )
264	        names = ("barrier_in", "transfer", "barrier_out", "copy_out")
265	        return out, dict(zip(names, (float(v) for v in stages), strict=True))
266	
267	    def destroy(self) -> None:
268	        """Release the group's windows and its transfer stream. Collective: dropping a window is.
269	        Buffers from ``empty_output()`` are unaffected -- they are yours."""
270	        if self._destroyed:
271	            return
272	        # Drain the comm stream first: dist.barrier only syncs the caller's current stream, so an
273	        # unwaited async call could still be writing a window that is about to be freed.
274	        self._comm_stream.synchronize()
275	        dist.barrier(group=self.pg)
276	        self._handle.destroy()
277	        self._destroyed = True
278	
279	    def __del__(self) -> None:
280	        # A group that is dropped rather than destroyed still has to outlive its own transfers.
281	        # The handle's C++ destructor waits on the internal transfer stream but knows nothing of
282	        # this one, so an unwaited async call could still be writing a window as it is freed.
283	        # There is no barrier here on purpose: a finalizer is no place for a collective, which is
284	        # why destroy() and not this is the supported path.
285	        if not self._destroyed:
286	            self._comm_stream.synchronize()

1	# API
2	
3	Shapes: `b` batch, `d` head dim, `ws` world size. `s_local` / `n_local` are this rank's sequence
4	and head shard; `s_global = sum(seq_splits)`, `n_global = sum(head_splits)`.
5	
6	## Collective contract
7	
8	Violating these hangs the group. Nothing raises and nothing times out.
9	
10	- **Every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes.** A window is allocated on the first call
11	  that needs one, and that allocation is collective.
12	- **Construction, `empty_output()` and `destroy()` are collective** over `process_group`.
13	- **Every rank must issue the same sequence of dtypes**, for the same reason as shapes: a window is
14	  allocated per `(role, dtype)`.
15	- **With autograd, every rank's engine must reach the backward node in the same order.** In
16	  sequence parallelism it does, because every rank runs the same graph — but it is a new way to
17	  hang, and the graph holds the group alive, so a graph replayed after `destroy()` raises.
18	- **One buffer, one call at a time.** A call overwrites the buffer it writes into, so two
19	  concurrent calls need two `empty_output()` buffers — or `all_to_all_4d_async(lend=True)`, which
20	  keeps the buffers itself and rotates through them.
21	
22	## `UlyssesGroup(process_group=None, device=None, *, require_nvlink=True)`
23	
24	| Parameter | Meaning |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| `process_group` | The group to run over; `None` uses `dist.group.WORLD`. Any subgroup works — there is no restriction on which ranks it contains. |
27	| `device` | This rank's CUDA device; `None` uses the current device. |
28	| `require_nvlink` | Refuse a group whose GPUs are not all NVLink-joined. `False` is for measuring that case, not for running in it. |
29	
30	The NVLink check reads the link type from NVML. Both a direct GPU-to-GPU link and two GPUs on one
31	NVSwitch fabric count. The check **fails open**: when NVML cannot answer — it is missing, or one
32	device cannot be probed — the group is built with no refusal and no warning, so a PCIe group on
33	such a machine runs, slowly, instead of being caught here. It is also skipped when two ranks share
34	a GPU, which is not a topology it can say anything about.
35	
36	## `fast_ulysses.nvlink_matrix(devices) -> dict[(int, int), bool] | None`
37	
38	The same probe, on its own: for a list of CUDA device indices, which ordered pairs are NVLink-joined.
39	`None` when NVML cannot answer at all. Not collective, and it takes no group — `fast-ulysses doctor`
40	prints it as a matrix.
41	
42	## `all_to_all_4d(x, *, mode=0, out=None, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None) -> Tensor`
43	
44	| mode | input | output |
45	| --- | --- | --- |
46	| 0 — scatter heads, gather sequence | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` |
47	| 1 — the inverse | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` |
48	
49	`x` is 4D CUDA, one of `float16` / `bfloat16` / `float32` / `float8_e4m3fn` / `float8_e5m2` /
50	`int8` / `uint8`, with `d * elem_size` 16-byte aligned; `.contiguous()` is applied internally.
51	Note the alignment rule tightens as the element shrinks: `d % 8` at float16, `d % 4` at float32,
52	`d % 16` at float8 and int8. Nothing below the check is dtype-specific — the transport moves bytes.
53	
54	**Differentiable, except with `out=`.** The vjp of a permutation is the inverse permutation, so the
55	backward is the other `mode` with the **same** splits. `all_to_all_single`'s backward swaps its
56	split sizes, because those describe one call's send and receive counts; `seq_splits` /
57	`head_splits` describe the group's geometry, which holds whichever way the data moves. Backward
58	always takes the copying path, never `out=`.
59	
60	A **meta** kernel propagates shapes under `FakeTensor` and AOTAutograd. `torch.compile` over a
61	module that holds an `UlyssesGroup` still graph-breaks: the group is a torchbind object with no
62	registered fake class. `empty_output()` refuses to be traced at all, with a message saying why.
63	
64	**Forward-mode AD works; reverse-mode `torch.func` does not.** A dual input carries its tangent
65	through a second collective, so `torch.autograd.forward_ad`, `torch.func.jvp` and
66	`torch.func.linearize` all run, at twice the traffic. `grad` / `vjp` / `jacrev` raise on their own:
67	the backward is a C++ `torch::autograd::Function`, which functorch cannot lift. `vmap` raises by an
68	explicit check on a batched input — it would run the collective once per batch element, so ranks
69	that disagree on the batch size would issue different numbers of collectives and hang. `jacfwd`
70	raises through that same check, being `vmap` over `jvp`. Map over the batch axis by reshaping it
71	into `b`, which the collective already carries.
72	
73	**`out`** decides the speed:
74	
75	- **absent, or a plain tensor of the output shape** — the transfer lands in a window this group
76	  keeps, and one flat device-to-device copy moves it out. The result is the caller's, with no
77	  lifetime rules.
78	- **a buffer from `empty_output()`** — the peers write it directly and there is no copy-out. Still
79	  the caller's own buffer, so still no lifetime rules; it is simply overwritten by the next call
80	  that uses it, like any output buffer.
81	
82	**`out` is not differentiable, and raises rather than dropping the gradient.** It reaches a
83	mutating op with no autograd formula, so the result is the buffer itself — `grad_fn` is `None`.
84	Returning that quietly would be indistinguishable from a caller who wanted no gradient, so a
85	grad-requiring input under grad mode raises instead. Use `out=` in inference or under
86	`torch.no_grad()`, where it is accepted; use the plain call inside a training graph.
87	
88	**`seq_splits[p]` / `head_splits[p]`** are rank p's sequence and head shard. Pass **both or
89	neither**, identical on every rank, matching the shape handed in. Neither means even shards, and
90	the scattered axis must then divide (`n_global % ws` for mode 0, `s_global % ws` for mode 1). Both
91	lets shards differ arbitrarily, which is what lets a caller drop sequence padding.
92	
93	### Raises
94	
95	`RuntimeError`, from validation that runs **before the call's first barrier**, so a rejected
96	argument leaves no rank waiting on peers that did not reject it: the group already `destroy()`ed;
97	`x` not 4D or not CUDA, or on a device other than the group's; dtype not in the dtype list above;
98	`d * elem_size` not 16 B-aligned; `mode` not 0 or 1; one of the splits without the other, or splits
99	contradicting `x`'s shape; no splits and the scattered axis does not divide; every rank's shard
100	empty, so the call moves no data; `out` not contiguous CUDA, on another device, or its dtype or
101	shape not the output's; `x` overlapping the window, or `out` partially overlapping it.
102	
103	`world_size` outside `[1, 8]` is refused by the constructor, so no call reaches it.
104	
105	## `all_to_all_4d_async(x, *, mode=0, out=None, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None, lend=False)`
106	
107	The same call on the group's high-priority comm stream, returning immediately.
108	
109	**Not differentiable, and it refuses rather than pretending.** An `AsyncCollectiveTensor` is built
110	with `requires_grad` on the wrapper, which makes it a leaf: autograd runs above the subclass and
111	never sees the wrapped tensor's history, so a `backward()` through it would run to completion and
112	leave `x.grad` as `None`. A grad-requiring input raises instead. Use `all_to_all_4d`.
113	
114	The result is an `AsyncCollectiveTensor`: `.wait()` returns the plain tensor, and so does the **first use by any
115	aten op** — either way the caller's stream waits on the comm stream's completion event GPU-side,
116	and the host does not block. A **view op** does not wait; it re-wraps.
117	
118	**Wait on, or use, every result.** A dropped one leaves its entry in torch's work registry and its
119	CUDA event behind; torch prints a count of the survivors at exit. `out=` is the hole, since reading
120	your own `out` never touches the registry — read the returned wrapper.
121	
122	The input is staged into a persistent per-`(shape, dtype)` buffer on the caller's stream, so `x` is
123	never retained cross-stream. That costs one device copy per call. Buffers of one shape form a pool
124	of **4**, so that many same-shaped calls can be in flight before one waits for another to retire.
125	
126	### `lend=True`
127	
128	`out=`'s saving without a buffer of your own: the peers write a window the group holds, the result
129	**is** that window, and there is no copy-out. Mutually exclusive with `out=` — passing both raises.
130	Not differentiable, like the rest of this call.
131	
132	The group keeps **4 windows per dtype and takes them in order**, one per call. Which window a call
133	fills has to be the same on every rank, since the transfer addresses the peers through that window
134	and the barrier through its signal pad; a rotation driven by the call count is the same everywhere,
135	and anything read off local reference counts is not.
136	
137	So the bound is a rule, not a hint: **at most 4 lent results alive at once, and every rank must drop
138	them at the same point in its own program.** A fifth live one raises. A rank that dropped a result
139	its peers still hold does not raise — it fills a window they are not reading, which is the hang this
140	page opens with.
141	
142	Use it when a result is consumed and released within the step that issued it, which is what a
143	split q/k/v exchange does. Keep a result across steps and `empty_output()` with `out=` is the fit.
144	
145	On a libtorch with no `c10d::register_work` there is no registry to bind to, and this returns a
146	`CompletedHandle` instead: same `.wait()`, correct results, no overlap. A distinct type, so it is
147	visible.
148	
149	The sync and async calls do not share a window, so mixing them is safe.
150	
151	## `empty_output(x, *, mode=0, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None) -> Tensor`
152	
153	A buffer shaped like `all_to_all_4d(x, mode=...)`'s output, in symmetric memory. Passing it back as
154	`out=` removes the copy-out.
155	
156	**Collective**, so allocate outside the loop and reuse it. It is an ordinary tensor: keep it across
157	steps, free it when you like, and it may outlive the group.
158	
159	It is larger than it looks. Under uneven splits the window has to hold the **largest** rank's
160	output, because the peer offsets only line up while every rank allocates the same size; the tensor
161	you get is a view of that allocation's dense prefix.
162	
163	## `destroy() -> None`
164	
165	Releases the group's windows and its transfer stream. All ranks must call it together. Buffers
166	from `empty_output()` are unaffected — they are yours.
167	
168	## Environment
169	
170	Nothing is read from the environment on the collective path. On a machine whose Fabric Manager
171	cannot bind NVLink SHARP, NCCL needs `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`; that affects the `torch.distributed`
172	bootstrap, not this operator. See [install.md](install.md).

5	docs/api.md lists what raises. Nothing tested any of it: test_plan.py reaches build_plan through
6	a2a_plan_debug, which builds A2ADims by hand and never runs make_dims or prepare, and

9	Every rejection here is checked on EVERY rank and the ranks then meet at a barrier. A check that
10	raised on some ranks and not others, or that raised after the call's first handshake, hangs this
11	worker instead of failing it, which is the failure mode worth catching.
12	
13	The aliasing guard compares against the window's CAPACITY rather than this call's requirement.
14	That is the conservative form, but only the case below is reachable through the public API: the
15	one window a caller can hold is an empty_output() buffer, and passing it as `out` takes the
16	zero-copy path, which is exempt by construction. A regression to the requirement form would
17	therefore not be caught here -- or anywhere -- so leave the capacity form alone.
18	
19	TWO GUARDS IN prepare() ARE UNREACHABLE FROM HERE, and it is worth writing down why so nobody
20	concludes they are untested by oversight. Both compare the window's byte size against what the
21	call needs, and reaching either requires an `out` that passes the shape and dtype checks above it
22	while sitting on an allocation too small in bytes:
23	
24	  - a smaller buffer fails the shape check first, so same-dtype reuse never gets that far;
25	  - a different-dtype view of the buffer needs `elem_size` times the bytes, and torch refuses to
26	    build it -- the storage is not resizable -- unless the window is strictly larger than this
27	    rank's output, which happens only under uneven splits. There the construction succeeds on the
28	    small-shard ranks and fails on the large one, so the call would be rank-dependent, and a
29	    rank-dependent `out` changes whether window() allocates: that is a collective, and the worker
30	    would hang rather than report.
31	
32	They are guards against a future caller, not against one that exists.
33	"""
34	
35	from __future__ import annotations
36	
37	import os
38	
39	import torch
40	import torch.distributed as dist
41	
42	from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup
43	
44	
45	class Rejects:
46	    def __init__(self, rank: int, ws: int) -> None:
47	        self.rank, self.ws, self.failed = rank, ws, 0
48	
49	    def raises(self, name: str, fragment: str, fn) -> None:
50	        """`fn` must raise, the message must contain `fragment`, and every rank must agree."""
51	        try:
52	            fn()
53	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- the type is torch's, the message is the contract
54	            if fragment not in str(exc):
55	                self.failed += 1
56	                print(f"FAIL rank={self.rank} {name}: raised, but not for the stated reason: {exc}")
57	            elif self.rank == 0:
58	                print(f"OK ws={self.ws} rejects {name}", flush=True)
59	        else:
60	            self.failed += 1
61	            print(f"FAIL rank={self.rank} {name}: accepted", flush=True)
62	        # If a rejection were not rank-uniform, or happened after the opening handshake, the ranks
63	        # would already be out of step and this is where it shows.
64	        dist.barrier()
65	
66	    def accepts(self, name: str, fn) -> None:
67	        """`fn` must NOT raise. For checking that a rejection left nothing broken behind."""
68	        try:
69	            fn()
70	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- any exception is the failure
71	            self.failed += 1
72	            print(f"FAIL rank={self.rank} {name}: {exc}", flush=True)
73	        else:
74	            if self.rank == 0:
75	                print(f"OK ws={self.ws} {name}", flush=True)
76	        dist.barrier()
77	
78	
79	def main() -> None:
80	    dist.init_process_group("nccl")
81	    rank, ws = dist.get_rank(), dist.get_world_size()
82	    torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", rank)))
83	    dev = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
84	
85	    group = UlyssesGroup(require_nvlink=False)
86	    check = Rejects(rank, ws)
87	    kw16 = {"dtype": torch.bfloat16, "device": dev}
88	
89	    good = torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws, 128, **kw16)
90	
91	    # --- shape, dtype and mode -----------------------------------------------------------
92	    check.raises(
93	        "a 3D input", "must be 4D", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(torch.randn(2, 16, 128, **kw16))
94	    )
95	    # float32 is SUPPORTED now; float64 stands in as a dtype that is still out.
96	    check.raises("float64", "dtype must be", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good.double()))
97	    check.raises("int32", "dtype must be", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good.to(torch.int32)))
98	    check.raises(

101	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws, 4, **kw16)),
102	    )

104	    check.raises(
105	        "a head dim that is aligned at bfloat16 but not at float8",
106	        "16-byte aligned",
107	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws, 8, **kw16).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)),
108	    )
109	    check.raises("mode 2", "mode must be 0 or 1", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=2))
110	    check.raises("a CPU input", "must be a CUDA tensor", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good.cpu()))
111	
112	    # --- splits ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
113	    check.raises(
114	        "one split list without the other",

117	    )

119	        "splits that contradict the shape",
120	        "but the splits imply",
121	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, seq_splits=[99] * ws, head_splits=[4] * ws),
122	    )

124	        odd = torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws + 1, 128, **kw16)
125	        check.raises(
126	            "a head axis that does not divide",
127	            "must divide world_size",
128	            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(odd),
129	        )

132	    check.raises(
133	        "a shape with nothing to exchange",
134	        "moves no data",
135	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(torch.empty(2, 16, 0, 128, **kw16)),
136	    )
137	    check.raises(
138	        "empty_output for a shape with nothing to exchange",
139	        "moves no data",
140	        lambda: group.empty_output(torch.empty(2, 0, 4 * ws, 128, **kw16)),
141	    )
142	
143	    # --- out= ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
144	    want_shape = (2, 16 * ws, 4, 128)
145	    check.raises(
146	        "out with the wrong shape",
147	        "out has shape",
148	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, out=torch.empty(2, 3, 4, 128, **kw16)),
149	    )
150	    check.raises(
151	        "out with the wrong dtype",
152	        "out has dtype",
153	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(
154	            good, out=torch.empty(*want_shape, dtype=torch.float16, device=dev)
155	        ),
156	    )
157	    check.raises(
158	        "a non-contiguous out",
159	        "contiguous CUDA tensor",
160	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, out=torch.empty(2, 16 * ws, 4, 256, **kw16)[..., ::2]),
161	    )
162	
163	    # --- the aliasing guard -----------------------------------------------------------------
164	    # The one shape a caller can actually reach: `out` is a window from empty_output(), so the
165	    # peers write it directly, and the input is a view of that SAME window. Reshaping the window
166	    # to the input whose output shape is exactly the window's shape works at any world size,
167	    # unlike feeding it back in as itself, whose two shapes only coincide at ws == 1.
168	    window = group.empty_output(good, mode=0)  # (2, 16*ws, 4, 128)
169	    check.raises(
170	        "an input that is a view of the window it fills",
171	        "input overlaps the window",
172	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(window.view(2, 16, 4 * ws, 128), mode=0, out=window),
173	    )
174	
175	    # --- autograd -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
176	    # The async result is an AsyncCollectiveTensor, which is a leaf: backward() through it would
177	    # run to completion and leave x.grad as None. Refused rather than silently wrong.
178	    check.raises(
179	        "an async call on an input that requires grad",
180	        "does not support autograd",
181	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good.detach().requires_grad_(True)),
182	    )
183	    # The out-variant mutates a buffer the caller already owns, so it carries no backward and the
184	    # value it returns is that buffer. Detaching silently would leave x.grad as None with nothing
185	    # to read it from, and the returned tensor cannot signal the difference either.
186	    check.raises(
187	        "an out= call on an input that requires grad",
188	        "does not support autograd",
189	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(
190	            good.detach().requires_grad_(True), out=torch.empty(*want_shape, **kw16)
191	        ),
192	    )
193	
194	    # --- torch.vmap --------------------------------------------------------------------------
195	    # Without a kernel on the batching key vmap does NOT fail: it falls back to a for-loop and

201	    batched = torch.randn(2, 2, 16, 4 * ws, 128, **kw16)
202	    out_buf = torch.empty(*want_shape, **kw16)
203	    frag = "does not support torch.vmap"
204	    check.raises(
205	        "vmap over the functional call",
206	        frag,
207	        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.all_to_all_4d(t, mode=0))(batched),
208	    )
209	    grad_src = good.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
210	    want_out = torch.empty(*want_shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
211	    # The LEGACY batching key, which torch.vmap does not use but two supported entry points do:
212	    # autograd.grad(is_grads_batched=True) and autograd.functional.jacobian(vectorize=True). A
213	    # registration that covered only functorch's key left these looping silently.
214	    check.raises(
215	        "autograd.grad(is_grads_batched=True)",
216	        frag,
217	        lambda: torch.autograd.grad(
218	            group.all_to_all_4d(grad_src, mode=0),
219	            grad_src,
220	            torch.stack([torch.randn_like(want_out) for _ in range(3)]),
221	            is_grads_batched=True,
222	        ),
223	    )
224	    check.raises(
225	        "vmap over the out= call",
226	        frag,
227	        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.all_to_all_4d(t, mode=0, out=out_buf))(batched),
228	    )
229	    check.raises(
230	        "vmap over the async call",
231	        frag,
232	        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.all_to_all_4d_async(t, mode=0).wait())(batched),
233	    )
234	    check.raises(
235	        "vmap over the async out= call",
236	        frag,
237	        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.all_to_all_4d_async(t, mode=0, out=out_buf).wait())(
238	            batched
239	        ),
240	    )
241	    check.raises(
242	        "vmap over empty_output",
243	        frag,
244	        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.empty_output(t, mode=0))(batched),
245	    )
246	    check.raises(
247	        "vmap over the timed call",
248	        frag,
249	        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group._timed(t, mode=0)[0])(batched),
250	    )
251	    # The LEGACY batching key, which is a second key and reaches the collective without functorch:
252	    # torch.autograd.grad(..., is_grads_batched=True) -- and torch.autograd.functional.* with
253	    # vectorize=True through it -- goes through torch._vmap_internals. Every check above enters
254	    # through functorch, so all six would still pass with that key unregistered, and the BACKWARD
255	    # would be the one looping a collective per row.
256	    grad_in = good.detach().requires_grad_(True)
257	    grad_out = group.all_to_all_4d(grad_in, mode=0)
258	    check.raises(
259	        "a batched grad_outputs, which is the legacy vmap",
260	        frag,
261	        lambda: torch.autograd.grad(
262	            grad_out,
263	            grad_in,
264	            grad_outputs=torch.ones(2, *want_shape, **kw16),
265	            is_grads_batched=True,
266	        ),
267	    )
268	
269	    # --- the plan cache must not answer for a call it never saw ------------------------------
270	    # An even-split call and an EMPTY-split one differ only in whether the lists are present. Held
271	    # as bare vectors the two keys were identical, so the second inherited the first's plan instead
272	    # of its own rejection. Warming the cache first is what makes this check mean anything.
273	    group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=0)
274	    check.raises(
275	        "empty split lists, after an even-split call cached its plan",
276	        "seq_splits has 0 entries",
277	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=0, seq_splits=[], head_splits=[]),
278	    )
279	
280	    # --- a tensor on another device -----------------------------------------------------------
281	    # The staging buffer takes the INPUT's device and is cached by shape and dtype alone, so before
282	    # the check moved ahead of stage() one wrong-device async call left a buffer on that device
283	    # behind and every later call for that shape copied across devices before failing. Both entry
284	    # points, because they check in different places: prepare() for the sync call, run_staged() for
285	    # the async one.
286	    other = torch.device("cuda", (dev.index + 1) % torch.cuda.device_count())
287	    if other != dev:
288	        stray = torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=other)
289	        check.raises(
290	            "an input on another device",
291	            "one group serves exactly one device",
292	            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(stray),
293	        )
294	        check.raises(
295	            "an async input on another device",
296	            "one group serves exactly one device",
297	            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(stray),
298	        )
299	        # The poisoning is what the check's placement fixes: the same shape has to still work.
300	        check.accepts(
301	            "the same shape after a wrong-device call",
302	            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good).wait(),
303	        )
304	        check.raises(
305	            "out on another device",
306	            "out is on cuda:",
307	            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(
308	                good, out=torch.empty(*want_shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=other)
309	            ),
310	        )
311	
312	    # --- inference mode -------------------------------------------------------------------------
313	    # The staging buffer outlives the call that allocates it, and one allocated under inference mode
314	    # stays an inference tensor: every later copy_ into it from outside raises, retiring that
315	    # (shape, dtype) for the group's lifetime. Both calls have to be accepted, and the SECOND is the
316	    # check -- the first only sets the trap.
317	    with torch.inference_mode():
318	        check.accepts(
319	            "an async call inside inference_mode", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good).wait()
320	        )
321	    check.accepts(
322	        "the same shape after an inference_mode call",
323	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good).wait(),
324	    )
325	    # --- lend=True's bound ----------------------------------------------------------------------
326	    # The rotation is fixed at four windows per dtype, so a fifth live result comes back to one a
327	    # caller still holds. REFUSED rather than absorbed: every softer answer -- wait for it, copy out
328	    # instead, allocate another -- is a decision this rank would make from its own reference counts,
329	    # and a rank that took it while its peers did not would fill a different window than they
330	    # addressed. Held in a list, since the check is that they are alive at the same time.
331	    held = [group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, lend=True).wait() for _ in range(4)]
332	    check.raises(
333	        "a fifth live lent result",
334	        "lent results may be alive at once",
335	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, lend=True).wait(),
336	    )
337	    del held
338	    check.accepts(
339	        "lend=True again once the earlier results are dropped",
340	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, lend=True).wait(),
341	    )
342	    # Both ask for the zero-copy path. Silently preferring one would leave a lend=True that did
343	    # nothing, on the argument whose whole purpose is to avoid owning a buffer.
344	    check.raises(
345	        "out= together with lend=True",
346	        "not both",
347	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, out=group.empty_output(good), lend=True),
348	    )
349	
350	    check.accepts(
351	        "out= inside no_grad on a grad-requiring input",

354	                good.detach().requires_grad_(True), out=group.empty_output(good)
355	            )
356	        )(),
357	    )
358	
359	    # --- a destroyed group --------------------------------------------------------------------

362	    # ran the entire collective on a destroyed group and rebuilt the transfer stream it had just

364	    dead_out = group.empty_output(good, mode=0)
365	    group.destroy()
366	    check.raises(
367	        "a zero-copy call on a destroyed group",

369	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=0, out=dead_out),
370	    )
371	    check.raises(
372	        "a copying call on a destroyed group",
373	        "has been destroyed",
374	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=0),
375	    )
376	    # The async path checks in run_staged rather than in prepare(), and it has to check BEFORE
377	    # stage(): destroy() returns early the second time, so a staging entry created after it is
378	    # never freed and its event leaks with the group.
379	    check.raises(
380	        "an async call on a destroyed group",
381	        "has been destroyed",
382	        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, mode=0),
383	    )

385	    verdict = torch.tensor([check.failed], device=dev)

388	        print("ALL PASS" if verdict.item() == 0 else f"FAILED {int(verdict.item())} checks")

    rank-dependent `out` changes whether window() allocates: that is a collective, and the worker
    would hang rather than report.

They are guards against a future caller, not against one that exists.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup


class Rejects:
    def __init__(self, rank: int, ws: int) -> None:
        self.rank, self.ws, self.failed = rank, ws, 0

    def raises(self, name: str, fragment: str, fn) -> None:
        """`fn` must raise, the message must contain `fragment`, and every rank must agree."""
        try:
            fn()
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- the type is torch's, the message is the contract
            if fragment not in str(exc):
                self.failed += 1
                print(f"FAIL rank={self.rank} {name}: raised, but not for the stated reason: {exc}")
            elif self.rank == 0:
                print(f"OK ws={self.ws} rejects {name}", flush=True)
        else:
            self.failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL rank={self.rank} {name}: accepted", flush=True)
        # If a rejection were not rank-uniform, or happened after the opening handshake, the ranks
        # would already be out of step and this is where it shows.
        dist.barrier()

    def accepts(self, name: str, fn) -> None:
        """`fn` must NOT raise. For checking that a rejection left nothing broken behind."""
        try:
            fn()
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- any exception is the failure
            self.failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL rank={self.rank} {name}: {exc}", flush=True)
        else:
            if self.rank == 0:
                print(f"OK ws={self.ws} {name}", flush=True)
        dist.barrier()


def main() -> None:
    dist.init_process_group("nccl")
    rank, ws = dist.get_rank(), dist.get_world_size()
    torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", rank)))
    dev = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())

    group = UlyssesGroup(require_nvlink=False)
    check = Rejects(rank, ws)
    kw16 = {"dtype": torch.bfloat16, "device": dev}

    good = torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws, 128, **kw16)

    # --- shape, dtype and mode -----------------------------------------------------------
    check.raises(
        "a 3D input", "must be 4D", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(torch.randn(2, 16, 128, **kw16))
    )
    # float32 is SUPPORTED now; float64 stands in as a dtype that is still out.
    check.raises("float64", "dtype must be", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good.double()))
    check.raises("int32", "dtype must be", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good.to(torch.int32)))
    check.raises(
        "a head dim that is not 16B-aligned",
        "16-byte aligned",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws, 4, **kw16)),
    )
    # The alignment rule tightens as the element shrinks: 8 halves are 16 B, 8 fp8 are 8 B.
    check.raises(
        "a head dim that is aligned at bfloat16 but not at float8",
        "16-byte aligned",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws, 8, **kw16).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)),
    )
    check.raises("mode 2", "mode must be 0 or 1", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=2))
    check.raises("a CPU input", "must be a CUDA tensor", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good.cpu()))

    # --- splits ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    check.raises(
        "one split list without the other",
        "both seq_splits and head_splits",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, seq_splits=[16] * ws),
    )
    check.raises(
        "splits that contradict the shape",
        "but the splits imply",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, seq_splits=[99] * ws, head_splits=[4] * ws),
    )
    if ws > 1:  # at ws == 1 every head count divides, so there is nothing to reject
        odd = torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws + 1, 128, **kw16)
        check.raises(
            "a head axis that does not divide",
            "must divide world_size",
            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(odd),
        )

    # --- an empty collective: window_numel would be 0, which is not an allocation ----------
    check.raises(
        "a shape with nothing to exchange",
        "moves no data",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(torch.empty(2, 16, 0, 128, **kw16)),
    )
    check.raises(
        "empty_output for a shape with nothing to exchange",
        "moves no data",
        lambda: group.empty_output(torch.empty(2, 0, 4 * ws, 128, **kw16)),
    )

    # --- out= ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    want_shape = (2, 16 * ws, 4, 128)
    check.raises(
        "out with the wrong shape",
        "out has shape",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, out=torch.empty(2, 3, 4, 128, **kw16)),
    )
    check.raises(
        "out with the wrong dtype",
        "out has dtype",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(
            good, out=torch.empty(*want_shape, dtype=torch.float16, device=dev)
        ),
    )
    check.raises(
        "a non-contiguous out",
        "contiguous CUDA tensor",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, out=torch.empty(2, 16 * ws, 4, 256, **kw16)[..., ::2]),
    )

    # --- the aliasing guard -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # The one shape a caller can actually reach: `out` is a window from empty_output(), so the
    # peers write it directly, and the input is a view of that SAME window. Reshaping the window
    # to the input whose output shape is exactly the window's shape works at any world size,
    # unlike feeding it back in as itself, whose two shapes only coincide at ws == 1.
    window = group.empty_output(good, mode=0)  # (2, 16*ws, 4, 128)
    check.raises(
        "an input that is a view of the window it fills",
        "input overlaps the window",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(window.view(2, 16, 4 * ws, 128), mode=0, out=window),
    )

    # --- autograd -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The async result is an AsyncCollectiveTensor, which is a leaf: backward() through it would
    # run to completion and leave x.grad as None. Refused rather than silently wrong.
    check.raises(
        "an async call on an input that requires grad",
        "does not support autograd",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good.detach().requires_grad_(True)),
    )
    # The out-variant mutates a buffer the caller already owns, so it carries no backward and the
    # value it returns is that buffer. Detaching silently would leave x.grad as None with nothing
    # to read it from, and the returned tensor cannot signal the difference either.
    check.raises(
        "an out= call on an input that requires grad",
        "does not support autograd",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(
            good.detach().requires_grad_(True), out=torch.empty(*want_shape, **kw16)
        ),
    )

    # --- torch.vmap --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Without a kernel on the batching key vmap does NOT fail: it falls back to a for-loop and
    # issues one collective per batch element, silently. Ranks whose batch sizes differ then issue
    # different numbers of collectives and hang -- the failure this library documents most loudly,
    # with nothing raised and nothing timed out. So the check is that the call RAISES; an
    # "accepted" here means the loop is back, and a torch that routes vmap through some other key
    # would show up the same way.
    batched = torch.randn(2, 2, 16, 4 * ws, 128, **kw16)
    out_buf = torch.empty(*want_shape, **kw16)
    frag = "does not support torch.vmap"
    check.raises(
        "vmap over the functional call",
        frag,
        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.all_to_all_4d(t, mode=0))(batched),
    )
    grad_src = good.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
    want_out = torch.empty(*want_shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    # The LEGACY batching key, which torch.vmap does not use but two supported entry points do:
    # autograd.grad(is_grads_batched=True) and autograd.functional.jacobian(vectorize=True). A
    # registration that covered only functorch's key left these looping silently.
    check.raises(
        "autograd.grad(is_grads_batched=True)",
        frag,
        lambda: torch.autograd.grad(
            group.all_to_all_4d(grad_src, mode=0),
            grad_src,
            torch.stack([torch.randn_like(want_out) for _ in range(3)]),
            is_grads_batched=True,
        ),
    )
    check.raises(
        "vmap over the out= call",
        frag,
        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.all_to_all_4d(t, mode=0, out=out_buf))(batched),
    )
    check.raises(
        "vmap over the async call",
        frag,
        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.all_to_all_4d_async(t, mode=0).wait())(batched),
    )
    check.raises(
        "vmap over the async out= call",
        frag,
        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.all_to_all_4d_async(t, mode=0, out=out_buf).wait())(
            batched
        ),
    )
    check.raises(
        "vmap over empty_output",
        frag,
        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group.empty_output(t, mode=0))(batched),
    )
    check.raises(
        "vmap over the timed call",
        frag,
        lambda: torch.vmap(lambda t: group._timed(t, mode=0)[0])(batched),
    )
    # The LEGACY batching key, which is a second key and reaches the collective without functorch:
    # torch.autograd.grad(..., is_grads_batched=True) -- and torch.autograd.functional.* with
    # vectorize=True through it -- goes through torch._vmap_internals. Every check above enters
    # through functorch, so all six would still pass with that key unregistered, and the BACKWARD
    # would be the one looping a collective per row.
    grad_in = good.detach().requires_grad_(True)
    grad_out = group.all_to_all_4d(grad_in, mode=0)
    check.raises(
        "a batched grad_outputs, which is the legacy vmap",
        frag,
        lambda: torch.autograd.grad(
            grad_out,
            grad_in,
            grad_outputs=torch.ones(2, *want_shape, **kw16),
            is_grads_batched=True,
        ),
    )

    # --- the plan cache must not answer for a call it never saw ------------------------------
    # An even-split call and an EMPTY-split one differ only in whether the lists are present. Held
    # as bare vectors the two keys were identical, so the second inherited the first's plan instead
    # of its own rejection. Warming the cache first is what makes this check mean anything.
    group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=0)
    check.raises(
        "empty split lists, after an even-split call cached its plan",
        "seq_splits has 0 entries",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=0, seq_splits=[], head_splits=[]),
    )

    # --- a tensor on another device -----------------------------------------------------------
    # The staging buffer takes the INPUT's device and is cached by shape and dtype alone, so before
    # the check moved ahead of stage() one wrong-device async call left a buffer on that device
    # behind and every later call for that shape copied across devices before failing. Both entry
    # points, because they check in different places: prepare() for the sync call, run_staged() for
    # the async one.
    other = torch.device("cuda", (dev.index + 1) % torch.cuda.device_count())
    if other != dev:
        stray = torch.randn(2, 16, 4 * ws, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=other)
        check.raises(
            "an input on another device",
            "one group serves exactly one device",
            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(stray),
        )
        check.raises(
            "an async input on another device",
            "one group serves exactly one device",
            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(stray),
        )
        # The poisoning is what the check's placement fixes: the same shape has to still work.
        check.accepts(
            "the same shape after a wrong-device call",
            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good).wait(),
        )
        check.raises(
            "out on another device",
            "out is on cuda:",
            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(
                good, out=torch.empty(*want_shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=other)
            ),
        )

    # --- inference mode -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The staging buffer outlives the call that allocates it, and one allocated under inference mode
    # stays an inference tensor: every later copy_ into it from outside raises, retiring that
    # (shape, dtype) for the group's lifetime. Both calls have to be accepted, and the SECOND is the
    # check -- the first only sets the trap.
    with torch.inference_mode():
        check.accepts(
            "an async call inside inference_mode", lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good).wait()
        )
    check.accepts(
        "the same shape after an inference_mode call",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good).wait(),
    )
    # --- lend=True's bound ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The rotation is fixed at four windows per dtype, so a fifth live result comes back to one a
    # caller still holds. REFUSED rather than absorbed: every softer answer -- wait for it, copy out
    # instead, allocate another -- is a decision this rank would make from its own reference counts,
    # and a rank that took it while its peers did not would fill a different window than they
    # addressed. Held in a list, since the check is that they are alive at the same time.
    held = [group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, lend=True).wait() for _ in range(4)]
    check.raises(
        "a fifth live lent result",
        "lent results may be alive at once",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, lend=True).wait(),
    )
    del held
    check.accepts(
        "lend=True again once the earlier results are dropped",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, lend=True).wait(),
    )
    # Both ask for the zero-copy path. Silently preferring one would leave a lend=True that did
    # nothing, on the argument whose whole purpose is to avoid owning a buffer.
    check.raises(
        "out= together with lend=True",
        "not both",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, out=group.empty_output(good), lend=True),
    )

    check.accepts(
        "out= inside no_grad on a grad-requiring input",
        lambda: torch.no_grad()(
            lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(
                good.detach().requires_grad_(True), out=group.empty_output(good)
            )
        )(),
    )

    # --- a destroyed group --------------------------------------------------------------------
    # `out` from empty_output() takes the zero-copy path, which reaches neither window() nor
    # make_output() -- the only two places that used to check. Without a check in prepare() this
    # ran the entire collective on a destroyed group and rebuilt the transfer stream it had just
    # torn down, leaking it. Held from before destroy(), since empty_output() checks too.
    dead_out = group.empty_output(good, mode=0)
    group.destroy()
    check.raises(
        "a zero-copy call on a destroyed group",
        "has been destroyed",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=0, out=dead_out),
    )
    check.raises(
        "a copying call on a destroyed group",
        "has been destroyed",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d(good, mode=0),
    )
    # The async path checks in run_staged rather than in prepare(), and it has to check BEFORE
    # stage(): destroy() returns early the second time, so a staging entry created after it is
    # never freed and its event leaks with the group.
    check.raises(
        "an async call on a destroyed group",
        "has been destroyed",
        lambda: group.all_to_all_4d_async(good, mode=0),
    )

    verdict = torch.tensor([check.failed], device=dev)
    dist.all_reduce(verdict)
    if rank == 0:
        print("ALL PASS" if verdict.item() == 0 else f"FAILED {int(verdict.item())} checks")
    dist.destroy_process_group()
    if verdict.item():
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Layout contract for the 4D all-to-all, checked without a GPU or a process group.

The plan is a list of pitched copies (src/a2a_plan.cc). Here we execute those
copies over plain byte buffers -- one symmetric window per simulated rank -- and compare the
result against the reference built from ``all_to_all_single`` + permute, which is the semantics
every Ulysses implementation agrees on. If this passes, the addressing is right and any later
failure is a transport or synchronisation bug, not a layout bug.

The window holds the whole output here: every rank sends its own share through it like any
other peer's. The zero-copy path returns that window as-is and the copying path moves all of it
out in one flat copy, so neither adds addressing this replay would have to model.
"""

import numpy as np
import pytest

torch = pytest.importorskip("torch")
# Importing the package registers torch.ops.fast_ulysses; a2a_plan_debug needs no GPU.
pytest.importorskip("fast_ulysses", reason="fast_ulysses._C extension not built")

SCATTER_HEAD = 0
GATHER_HEAD = 1

    output_shape, window_numel, ops = torch.ops.fast_ulysses.a2a_plan_debug(
        b, d, rank, world_size, list(seq_splits), list(head_splits), mode, elem_size
    )
    output_shape = list(output_shape)
    return {
        "output_shape": output_shape,
        "output_bytes": int(np.prod(output_shape)) * elem_size,
        "window_numel": int(window_numel),
        "ops": ops.numpy(),
    }


def apply_ops(ops, src, dst):
    for (
        _peer,
        src_off,
        dst_off,
        src_pitch,
        dst_pitch,
        width,
        rows,
        depth,
        src_slice,
        dst_slice,
    ) in ops:
        # depth folds the batch dimension into one op; replaying it is the same copy repeated
        # at a fixed stride, which is exactly what cudaMemcpy3DAsync does.
        for z in range(depth):
            for row in range(rows):
                s = src_off + z * src_slice + row * src_pitch
                t = dst_off + z * dst_slice + row * dst_pitch
                dst[t : t + width] = src[s : s + width]

    """Replay the device sequence on plain byte buffers: rank r writes into peer p's window."""
    windows = [np.zeros(p["output_bytes"], dtype=np.uint8) for p in plans]

```python
def output_shape(x_shape, mode, ws, rank=0, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None):
    b, x1, x2, d = x_shape
    if seq_splits is None:
        assert head_splits is None
        if mode == 0:
            seq_splits, head_splits = [x1] * ws, [x2 // ws] * ws
        else:
            seq_splits, head_splits = [x1 // ws] * ws, [x2] * ws
    s_global = sum(seq_splits)
    n_local = head_splits[rank]
    if mode == 0:
        return (b, s_global, n_local, d)
    return (b, seq_splits[rank], sum(head_splits), d)
```

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. **由输入形状与 mode 推出输出形状**：给一个 `(b, s, n, d)` 和 `mode=0/1`（以及可选的 splits），不运行任何代码就能写出输出的四维形状。
2. **解释 dtype 白名单与 16 字节对齐规则**：知道哪 7 种 dtype 被接受，理解为什么规则写成 `d * elem_size` 必须是 16 的倍数，以及它如何随元素变窄而收紧（fp16 要 `d % 8`、fp32 要 `d % 4`、fp8/int8 要 `d % 16`）。
3. **把 docs/api.md 的 Raises 清单逐条落到源码行**：每条文档化的 `RuntimeError` 都能指到是哪个文件的哪个 `TORCH_CHECK` 抛的，并理解「校验必须全部发生在第一个屏障之前」这条工程纪律。
4. **复述集体调用契约五条**（形状序列、dtype 序列、集合性操作、backward 顺序、一缓冲一调用），并解释为什么违反契约的后果是**挂起而非报错**——这五种违规没有任何一条会被 `try/except` 捕到。

本讲承上启下：u1-l2 讲了「为什么要有两次 all-to-all」，u2-l1 讲了「组怎么建」；本讲回答「一次调用合法地长什么样」——这是后面 u3（布局计划）、u4（窗口管理）一切源码的前置契约。

## 2. 前置知识

- **张量形状记号**：`b` 批大小、`s` 序列长度、`n` 注意力头数、`d` 每头维度、`ws` 世界大小（rank 数）。`s_local` / `n_local` 是本 rank 持有的分片，`s_global = sum(seq_splits)`、`n_global = sum(head_splits)` 是全组总量。
- **SPMD 与集合操作**（u1-l2、u2-l1 已建立）：所有 rank 执行同一段程序；`all_gather`、对称内存 rendezvous 这类操作要求**每个 rank 都到达**才有人推进。一个 rank 提前抛错退出、别人还在等它，就是「挂起」。
- **mode 0 / mode 1**（u1-l2 已建立）：mode 0 用「序列分片 × 全部头」换「完整序列 × 头分片」，mode 1 是它的严格逆变换。本讲只关心**形状怎么对应**，不关心数据怎么搬（那是 u3/u5 的事）。
- **TORCH_CHECK 与 RuntimeError**：torch C++ 源码里 `TORCH_CHECK(条件, 消息)` 在条件不满足时抛 `c10::Error`，穿过 pybind11 到 Python 就是 `RuntimeError`。本讲看到的每条报错都是它。
- **16 字节对齐的直觉**：GPU 拷贝引擎搬数据时按「行」拷，一行是 `d * elem_size` 个字节。硬件对 16 字节整数倍的地址/宽度有天然偏好（这关系到能否走最快的拷贝路径）。本讲只需记住：**库里所有拷贝的起点、步长、宽度都是 `d * elem_size` 的倍数，所以只要这一个数对齐，全部对齐**——一条检查覆盖整个计划。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 mode 形状表：由输入形状与 mode 推出输出形状

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`all_to_all_4d` 是一个**纯重排**：它不计算任何东西，只把「序列轴上的分片」和「头轴上的分片」互换角色。所以输出形状完全由输入形状、mode、以及（可选的）splits 决定——不需要看数据，甚至不需要 GPU。这份「形状推导规则」就是本模块要掌握的**形状契约**。

不传 splits 时是偶均分特例；传了 splits，`seq_splits[p]` / `head_splits[p]` 表示「rank p 拥有的序列片长 / 头片数」，这是**组几何**的描述，与数据向哪个方向流动无关（这个性质在 u6-l3 讲 backward 时会再次出现：backward 不交换 splits）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

记 \( s_{\text{global}} = \sum_p \text{seq\_splits}[p] \)，\( n_{\text{global}} = \sum_p \text{head\_splits}[p] \)，\( n_{\text{local}} = \text{head\_splits}[\text{rank}] \)，\( s_{\text{local}} = \text{seq\_splits}[\text{rank}] \)。

不传 splits 时，由形状反推偶均分：

- mode 0 输入 `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` → 推得 `seq_splits = [s_local]*ws`、`head_splits = [n_global/ws]*ws`
- mode 1 输入 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` → 推得 `seq_splits = [s_global/ws]*ws`、`head_splits = [n_local]*ws`

然后套用形状表：

| mode | 输入 | 输出 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 — 散头、聚序列 | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` |
| 1 — 逆变换 | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` |

推导顺序（伪代码）：

```text
resolve_splits(x_shape, mode, ws, splits?):
    if splits 缺失:
        mode 0: 要求 n_global % ws == 0；seq=[x1]*ws, head=[x2/ws]*ws
        mode 1: 要求 s_global % ws == 0；seq=[x1/ws]*ws, head=[x2]*ws
    else:
        两组都必须给，且与 x 的形状交叉吻合
    if mode == 0: return (b, sum(seq), head[rank], d)
    else:         return (b, seq[rank],  sum(head), d)
```

注意 `ws = 1` 的特例：`s_local == s_global`、`n_local == n_global`，两个 mode 的形状都退化成恒等——这就是为什么 u1-l3 说「world_size=1 是合法一等公民」，可以用它做单卡冒烟测试。

**实践目标**：不看文档、手写形状推导函数，再用真实调用验证。

```python
def output_shape(x_shape, mode, ws, rank=0, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None):
    b, x1, x2, d = x_shape
    if seq_splits is None:
        assert head_splits is None, "两组 splits 要么都传要么都不传"
```

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`ws=8`，输入 `(1, 4096, 40, 384)`，`mode=0`，不传 splits。会发生什么？

**答案**：mode 0 要求头轴整除：`n_global=40`，`40 % 8 == 0`，合法。推得 `seq_splits=[4096]*8`、`head_splits=[5]*8`，输出 `(1, 32768, 5, 384)`。若头数换成 44（`44 % 8 != 0`），则在 `make_dims` 抛 `RuntimeError`，消息以 `mode 0 scatters the head axis` 开头。

**练习 2**：mode 1 下输入 `(2, 128, 6, 64)`、`ws=4`、不传 splits，输出是什么？反过来把输出喂给 mode 0 会得到什么？

**答案**：mode 1 输入形状是 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)`，检查 `128 % 4 == 0`，推得 `seq_splits=[32]*4`、`head_splits=[6]*4`，输出 `(2, 32, 24, 64)`。把 `(2, 32, 24, 64)` 喂给 mode 0：检查 `24 % 4 == 0`，`seq_splits=[32]*4`、`head_splits=[6]*4`，输出 `(2, 128, 6, 64)`——还原成最初输入。两次调用互逆，这正是 u2-l4 示例里「包夹注意力」成立的前提。

**练习 3**：为什么 `ws=1` 时任何头数都不会触发整除检查的报错？

**答案**：任何整数对 1 取模都是 0。`make_dims` 的两个整除分支（`x2 % ws`、`x1 % ws`）在 `ws=1` 下恒真，所以该检查在单 rank 下「不可达」——这也是本讲综合实践中我们无法在 `ws=1` 下测整除报错的原因（test/distributed/validation.py:L123 对此有同样的备注）。

### 4.2 dtype 白名单与 16 字节对齐

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

传输层搬运的是**字节**，不理解数值含义——`build_plan` 只接收一个 `elem_size`，窗口和 plan 缓存的键里带 dtype，仅此而已。既然如此，为什么要限制 dtype？

因为「接受哪些类型」是一个**产品决策而非技术约束**：源码注释明确说这是「listed, not opened up」（列出来的，不是推导出来的）。放行 `kBool`、复数、量化类型意味着要为这些没人推理过的类型背书。于是白名单收下训练里实际会用的 7 种：`float16 / bfloat16 / float32 / float8_e4m3fn / float8_e5m2 / int8 / uint8`。

对齐规则 `d * elem_size` 必须是 16 的倍数，来自传输的物理形态：拷贝引擎按「一行 `d * elem_size` 字节」做二维/三维拷贝（u3、u5 展开），所有偏移、步长、宽度都是这个数的倍数。**检查一行，对齐全局**——这是把一条约束放在最便宜位置（纯主机、进 plan 缓存键）的典型设计。

注意规则的**不对称收紧**：约束的是字节数不是维数，所以元素越窄，对 `d` 的要求越苛刻。fp16 要 `d % 8 == 0`，fp32 只需 `d % 4 == 0`，fp8/int8 则要 `d % 16 == 0`。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

被接受的 dtype 与对应的对齐要求：

| dtype | elem_size | 对 `d` 的要求 | 例：`d=128` | 例：`d=8` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| float16 | 2 B | \( d \times 2 \equiv 0 \pmod{16} \Rightarrow d \bmod 8 = 0 \) | ✅ 256 B | ✅ 16 B |
| bfloat16 | 2 B | `d % 8 == 0` | ✅ | ✅ |
| float32 | 4 B | `d % 4 == 0` | ✅ | ✅ |
| float8_e4m3fn / float8_e5m2 | 1 B | `d % 16 == 0` | ✅ | ❌ 8 B |
| int8 / uint8 | 1 B | `d % 16 == 0` | ✅ | ❌ 8 B |

检查流程（`make_dims` 内，进入 splits 逻辑之前）：

```text
取 d = sizes[3]，elem = elementSize(dtype)
检查 (d * elem) % 16 == 0
    失败 → "the head dim must be 16-byte aligned: d=.. x .. B is .. B"
```

一个直接推论：`d=8` 在 bfloat16 下合法、转成 float8_e4m3fn 后非法——同一个形状在不同 dtype 下对齐结论不同，test/distributed/validation.py:L103-L108 专门测了这一条。

```cpp
// dst_offset, width, both pitches, the batch strides -- is a multiple of d * elem. Note the
// rule TIGHTENS as the element shrinks: d % 8 at fp16, d % 4 at fp32, d % 16 at fp8 and int8.
```

注意位置：这两条检查都在 `make_dims` 里，而 `make_dims` 只在 **plan 缓存未命中**时运行（见 [src/group.cc:L182-L195](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L182-L195)）。这不会有漏洞，因为「这里检查的每一样东西都是 plan 缓存键的一部分」——同一组 `(sizes, mode, dtype, splits)` 上次通过了检查，缓存命中直接复用是安全的（注释在 [src/group.cc:L39-L44](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L39-L44)）。

#### 4.2.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：把对齐表内化成可运行的判定器。

1. 实践目标：写一个 `head_dims_ok(d, dtype)`，对 `d ∈ {4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 96, 128}` × 全部 7 种 dtype 打一张 ✅/❌ 表。
2. 操作步骤（示例代码，纯主机）：


#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`d=6` 的 bfloat16 张量（`6×2=12` B）会被接受吗？`d=6` 的 float32（`6×4=24` B）呢？

**答案**：bfloat16：12 不是 16 的倍数，拒绝；float32：24 同样不是 16 的倍数，也拒绝。容易错以为是「`d` 是不是 2 的幂」的问题——判据始终是**字节数** `d * elem_size` 对 16 取模。

**练习 2**：为什么检查放在 `make_dims`（plan 缓存键的一部分）而不是每次调用都查的 `prepare` 里？

**答案**：因为对齐与否只依赖 `(sizes, dtype)`，而这两者连同 mode、splits 一起构成 plan 缓存键：同一组值一旦通过检查并缓存，后续命中不可能携带未检查的新值。相反，依赖**张量本身**而非形状的检查（是否 CUDA、是否连续、与窗口是否重叠）无法进缓存键，必须留在 `prepare` 每次调用执行——这正是 [src/group.cc:L39-L44](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L39-L44) 注释划分的两类。

**练习 3**：一个 `d=8` 的 bfloat16 张量 `.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)` 后再调用，两次的对齐结论分别是什么？

**答案**：bfloat16 下 `8×2=16` B，合法；转 float8 后 `8×1=8` B，在 `make_dims` 抛 `RuntimeError`（消息含 `16-byte aligned`）。dtype 变了、形状没变，但规则跟着**字节**走——validation.py 把这条作为独立用例（"a head dim that is aligned at bfloat16 but not at float8"）。

### 4.3 Raises 清单：每条拒绝对应哪里，为何都在第一个屏障之前

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

docs/api.md 的 Raises 一节列出了所有文档化的 `RuntimeError`。本模块做三件事：**逐条落到源码**、**理解排序原则**、**认清它的边界**。

排序原则是本讲最重要的一条工程纪律：**全部校验必须发生在调用的第一个屏障之前**。原因：这是一次集合调用。如果 rank 0 的参数非法、rank 1 的合法，而非法问题在「rank 0 已经进入第一个屏障、开始等所有人」之后才被发现——rank 0 抛错退出，rank 1 永远等下去。所以 `prepare` 的第一句注释就是「Everything here runs BEFORE the call's first barrier, so a rejected argument leaves no rank waiting on peers that did not reject it」（被拒的参数不会留下任何 rank 干等没拒它的同伴）。

边界：这份清单只覆盖**本 rank 单方面可判定**的非法性。需要跨 rank 一致性才能判定的（形状序列、dtype 序列……）属于 4.4 的契约，那里**没有**报错，只有挂起。两节合起来是同一枚硬币的两面：能本地判定的 → 提前抛；只能靠约定的 → 写进契约。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

`prepare` 的校验链（严格顺序，箭头后是被拒的后果）：

```text
check_alive()            → "this UlyssesGroup has been destroyed"
prune_owned()            （回收缓冲，不抛）
require_cuda(input)      → "input must be a CUDA tensor, got one on cpu"
require_group_device()   → "input is on cuda:X but this UlyssesGroup was built for cuda:Y"
input.contiguous()       （接受非连续输入，内部拷平）
group->plan(...)         → make_dims 的五连：
                             4D 检查 / dtype 白名单 / 16B 对齐 / mode ∈ {0,1} / splits 检查
out 分支（若有 out）      → contiguous CUDA / 设备 / dtype / 形状 四连
窗口获取 window()         → allocate()："this call moves no data"（全 rank 分片为空）
重叠检查                 → "input overlaps the window" / "out overlaps the window"
────────── 以上全部完成，才发出第一个屏障 fast_barrier ──────────
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

[src/bindings.cc:L87-L88](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/bindings.cc#L87-L88)
```cpp

```

```cpp
// a null data_ptr, which rendezvous refuses with a null handle.
TORCH_CHECK(numel > 0,
            "this call moves no data: every rank's shard is empty. ...");
```

`out` 的四连检查与重叠检查（消息见 4.3.2 流程图；源码在 [src/bindings.cc:L112-L139](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/bindings.cc#L112-L139) 与 [src/bindings.cc:L158-L172](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/bindings.cc#L158-L172)）。重叠检查用**字节区间**而非指针相等，因为部分重叠可以落在窗口基址之后；`out` **本身就是**窗口（来自 `empty_output` 的零拷贝路径）是唯一合法的重合。

### 4.4 集体调用契约：五条规则与「挂起而非报错」

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

4.3 的 Raises 清单保护的是「单 rank 可判定」的非法性。但一次集合调用的正确性还依赖**所有 rank 互相配合**：大家发同样形状的序列、同样 dtype 的序列、在同样的位置做集合操作。这类违规，任何一个 rank **单看自己的参数都发现不了**——rank 0 无法知道 rank 1 传了什么形状。既然查不出来，库的选择是不查：把要求写成契约，违反的后果是挂起。

[docs/api.md:L8](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L8) 一句话定调：**「Violating these hangs the group. Nothing raises and nothing times out.」**（违反这些会把组挂死。没有任何报错，也没有超时。）

为什么是挂起？以「形状序列不一致」为例：rank 0 先发 `(2,16,40,128)`，rank 1 先发 `(2,16,48,128)`。新形状触发窗口分配，分配需要 rendezvous——每个 rank 都要带着同样大小的窗口到场。rank 0 在等 rank 1 的句柄，rank 1 在等 rank 0 的，谁也等不到，GPU 上的自旋屏障永远转不出去，进程不退出、不抛错、不超时。这不是 bug，是集合操作的本质：**约定无法被单方面验证时，违反约定的代价由死锁承担**。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

契约五条（[docs/api.md:L10-L20](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L10-L20)），按「谁依赖它」理解：

```text
① 同形状序列   —— 首次遇新形状会触发集合性窗口分配（rendezvous）
② 集合性操作   —— 构造、empty_output()、destroy() 全组到齐才推进
③ 同 dtype 序列 —— 窗口按 (role, dtype) 缓存：dtype 序列不同 = 分配序列不同
④ backward 顺序 —— 反向节点里也要发集合通信，autograd 引擎到达顺序必须全组一致
⑤ 一缓冲一调用 —— 窗口是单缓冲：一次调用会覆盖它写过的缓冲
```

违反的后果统一：

```text
某 rank 单方面偏离契约
  → 它与同伴在某个集合点（rendezvous / 屏障 / all_gather）上失配
  → 对方永远等不到它，或它永远等不到对方
  → 进程挂起：无异常、无超时、无堆栈
```

判别准则（和 4.3 的分界线）：

- 违规**只涉及本 rank 的参数与本地状态**（形状不是 4D、dtype 不在白名单、组已 destroy……）→ Raises 清单，屏障前抛 `RuntimeError`。
- 违规**只有对比其他 rank 才能确认**（形状序列、dtype 序列、调用次数、释放时机……）→ 契约，挂起。

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

契约原文：[docs/api.md:L6-L20](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L6-L20)。

①③ 的根源——窗口按 `(role, dtype)` 缓存、按需增长，增长即集合分配：

[src/group.cc:L255-L267](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L255-L267)

```cpp
{
    check_alive();
    const auto key = std::make_pair(static_cast<int64_t>(role), dtype);
    auto       it  = windows_.find(key);
    if (it != windows_.end() && it->second.numel >= numel) {
        return it->second;
    }
    ...
    return windows_.emplace(key, allocate(numel, dtype)).first->second;
}
```
窗口装不下时调用 `allocate`，而 `allocate` 内部是 `empty_strided_p2p` + `rendezvous`（[src/group.cc:L218-L227](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L218-L227)）——rendezvous 要求每个 rank 带同样大小的分配到场。所以「同形状序列」「同 dtype 序列」不是风格建议，是 rendezvous 的物理前提（u4-l1、u4-l2 展开）。

⑤ 的根源——窗口是单缓冲，写者要先等读者：

[src/bindings.cc:L198-L203](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/bindings.cc#L198-L203)

```cpp
// call is about to overwrite what the previous one produced, which a peer may still be
// reading; the closing barrier below proves everyone's WRITES landed and nothing about their
// READS. ...
fast_barrier(stream, call.win->flag_ptrs, rank);
```
一次调用会覆盖上一次写进窗口的数据。同一个 `empty_output` 缓冲被两个并发的调用同时用作 `out=`，两边都在写同一块内存——屏障只保证「写都落地」，不保证「没人还在读」。所以要两条缓冲（或用 `lend=True` 让库自己轮转，u4-l4 展开）。

④ 的根源——backward 里真的有一次集合通信：

[src/bindings.cc:L549-L559](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/bindings.cc#L549-L559)

```cpp
// The copying form, never `out` from empty_output(): that is a collective allocation, and
// putting one inside backward would hand the rendezvous position to the autograd engine's
// node order rather than to the caller's own program. ...
return {at::Tensor(),
        A2AFunction::apply(group, grads[0].contiguous(), 1 - mode, seq, head),
        ...};
```

反向传播执行到 `A2AFunction::backward` 时会再发一次 `all_to_all_4d`（`1 - mode`，同一组 splits——u6-l3 展开）。如果各 rank 的 autograd 引擎以不同顺序到达这个节点，等于发出不同顺序的集合调用——回到契约①③的挂起。注释还说明了另一层：这也是 backward **永不走 `out=`** 的原因（把集合分配塞进 backward，rendezvous 的位置就交给了引擎的节点顺序）。

② 集合性操作：`empty_output` 走 `make_output` → `allocate`（rendezvous），`destroy` 在 [python/fast_ulysses/group.py:L267-L277](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L267-L277) 先排空 comm 流再 `dist.barrier`——全组到齐才能释放窗口。

最后看 Python 门面上一条「主动报错」而非挂起的边界案例——`out=` 遇到需要梯度的输入：

[src/bindings.cc 之上，python/fast_ulysses/group.py:L138-L143](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L138-L143)

```python
    raise RuntimeError(

        "op with no backward, so the gradient would be dropped without an error. Drop "
        "out=, or run under torch.no_grad()."

```
这条违规本可以静默（梯度悄悄丢失），库选择报错——「拒绝而非静默出错」是贯穿整个 API 的另一条价值观：**可检测的静默错误都升格为报错；不可检测的跨 rank 失配才留给契约**。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：源码阅读型实践——为三个违规场景指出违反的契约条目，并解释为什么不会有报错。

1. 实践目标：把「症状 → 契约条目 → 挂起机制」连起来。
2. 操作步骤：阅读 [docs/api.md:L6-L20](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L6-L20) 与 4.4.3 的源码，回答下面三个场景（先自己写，再对答案）：
   - 场景 A：`ws=2`，rank 0 循环里发 `(2, 16, 40, 128)`，rank 1 发 `(2, 16, 48, 128)`。
   - 场景 B：训练循环里，两个 rank 的 loss 里把两个用到 `all_to_all_4d` 的分支按不同顺序写了（rank 0 先分支甲后分支乙，rank 1 相反），前向无异常。
   - 场景 C：`buf = group.empty_output(x, mode=0)`，同一个循环迭代里把它同时作为两次不同 `all_to_all_4d(..., out=buf)` 的输出。
3. 需要观察的现象（纸面推演；**不要**真的在多卡上跑场景 A/B——那会挂死你的 GPU 进程，需要手工 kill）。
4. 预期结果：见答案。有 GPU 想安全体验「挂起」时，只可用 `--nproc_per_node=1` 验证「合法调用不挂」，跨 rank 失配在单卡上无法复现（这正是它危险的原因）。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1（对应 4.4.4 场景 A）**：违反哪条？为什么挂的是 rendezvous？

**答案**：违反①（同形状序列）。两个形状都没问题、dtype 也合法——每个 rank 单看都「合法」，所以 4.3 的检查全放行。第一个新形状触发窗口分配：rank 0 以 `window_numel(40 头方案)` 分配，rank 1 以 `window_numel(48 头方案)` 分配，rendezvous 上互相等对方的句柄，永远等不到。无异常、无超时。

**练习 2（对应场景 B）**：违反哪条？为什么前向没事、反向才挂？

**答案**：违反④（backward 顺序）。前向两次调用的**集合**在两个 rank 上次序一致（各自程序里都发了甲、乙两次，顺序无关紧要——只要形状序列与 dtype 序列相同）。挂起发生在反向：`A2AFunction::backward` 里各有一次集合通信（`1-mode` 调用），rank 0 的引擎先到甲的节点、rank 1 先到乙的节点，反向集合的到达顺序失配，屏障上互等。docs/api.md:L15-L17 特别提醒「这是全新的挂法」，且计算图持有 group 的引用——图活得比 `destroy()` 长还会再抛错。

**练习 3（对应场景 C）**：违反哪条？为什么可能「看起来还能跑」而更危险？

**答案**：违反⑤（一缓冲一调用）。`buf` 是同一块对称内存，两次调用都在让 peers 直写它。屏障保证的是「本次调用的写全部落地」，不保证「上一次的读者已经读完」；两个写者交错覆盖，结果是**损坏的数据而非崩溃**——最坏的一类失败，因为它可能安静地污染训练。修复：两个 `empty_output` 缓冲各配一次调用，或改用 `all_to_all_4d_async(lend=True)` 让库自己轮转四个窗口（u4-l4）。

```python
pytest.importorskip("fast_ulysses", reason="fast-ulysses._C extension not built")
```

## 6. 本讲小结

- **形状契约**：mode 0 把 `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` 变成 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)`，mode 1 是严格逆变换；不传 splits 时由被散射轴的整除性反推偶均分。输出形状可纯手推，`ws=1` 时退化为恒等。
- **dtype 与对齐**：7 种 dtype 的白名单是产品决策（传输只搬字节）；对齐约束是 `d * elem_size` 为 16 的倍数——一行检查覆盖 plan 里全部字节量，并随元素变窄而收紧（`d%8`/`d%4`/`d%16`）。
- **Raises 的排序纪律**：所有校验（销毁、设备、4D、dtype、对齐、mode、splits、out、重叠、空分片）都发生在第一个屏障之前——被拒的参数不会留下任何 rank 干等同伴；且「查形状的」进 plan 缓存键、「查张量的」留在每次调用。
- **契约五条与挂起**：形状序列、dtype 序列、集合性操作、backward 顺序、一缓冲一调用——跨 rank 才能判定的违规不设检查，违反即挂起（无异常、无超时）；能单方面判定的静默错误（如 `out=` 丢梯度）则升格为显式报错。
- **分界线**：`RuntimeError` 清单保护「本 rank 可判定」的世界；契约保护「全组一致」的世界。写分布式代码时的自查顺序永远是：先对照 Raises 排本地非法，再对照五条排跨 rank 失配。

# u2-l2 · all_to_all_4d 的形状契约与错误检查

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. **由输入形状与 mode 推出输出形状**：给一个 `(b, s, n, d)` 和 `mode=0/1`（以及可选的 splits），不运行任何代码就能写出输出的四维形状。
2. **解释 dtype 白名单与 16 字节对齐规则**：知道哪 7 种 dtype 被接受，理解为什么规则写成 `d * elem_size` 必须是 16 的倍数，以及它如何随元素变窄而收紧（fp16 要 `d % 8`、fp32 要 `d % 4`、fp8/int8 要 `d % 16`）。
3. **把 docs/api.md 的 Raises 清单逐条落到源码行**：每条文档化的 `RuntimeError` 都能指到是哪个文件的哪个 `TORCH_CHECK` 抛的，并理解「校验必须全部发生在第一个屏障之前」这条工程纪律。
4. **复述集体调用契约五条**（形状序列、dtype 序列、集合性操作、backward 顺序、一缓冲一调用），并解释为什么违反契约的后果是**挂起而非报错**——这五种违规没有任何一条会被 `try/except` 捕到。

本讲承上启下：u1-l2 讲了「为什么要有两次 all-to-all」，u2-l1 讲了「组怎么建」；本讲回答「一次调用合法地长什么样」——这是后面 u3（布局计划）、u4（窗口管理）一切源码的前置契约。

## 2. 前置知识

- **张量形状记号**：`b` 批大小、`s` 序列长度、`n` 注意力头数、`d` 每头维度、`ws` 世界大小（rank 数）。`s_local` / `n_local` 是本 rank 持有的分片，`s_global = sum(seq_splits)`、`n_global = sum(head_splits)` 是全组总量。
- **SPMD 与集合操作**（u1-l2、u2-l1 已建立）：所有 rank 执行同一段程序；`all_gather`、对称内存 rendezvous 这类操作要求**每个 rank 都到达**才有人推进。一个 rank 提前抛错退出、别人还在等它，就是「挂起」。
- **mode 0 / mode 1**（u1-l2 已建立）：mode 0 用「序列分片 × 全部头」换「完整序列 × 头分片」，mode 1 是它的严格逆变换。本讲只关心**形状怎么对应**，不关心数据怎么搬（那是 u3/u5 的事）。
- **TORCH_CHECK 与 RuntimeError**：torch C++ 源码里 `TORCH_CHECK(条件, 消息)` 在条件不满足时抛 `c10::Error`，穿过 pybind11 到 Python 就是 `RuntimeError`。本讲看到的每条报错都是它。
- **16 字节对齐的直觉**：GPU 拷贝引擎搬数据时按「行」拷，一行是 `d * elem_size` 个字节。硬件对 16 字节整数倍的地址/宽度有天然偏好（这关系到能否走最快的拷贝路径）。本讲只需记住：**库里所有拷贝的起点、步长、宽度都是 `d * elem_size` 的倍数，所以只要这一个数对齐，全部对齐**——一条检查覆盖整个计划。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 mode 形状表：由输入形状与 mode 推出输出形状

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`all_to_all_4d` 是一个**纯重排**：它不计算任何东西，只把「序列轴上的分片」和「头轴上的分片」互换角色。所以输出形状完全由输入形状、mode、以及（可选的）splits 决定——不需要看数据，甚至不需要 GPU。这份「形状推导规则」就是本模块要掌握的**形状契约**。

不传 splits 时是偶均分特例；传了 splits，`seq_splits[p]` / `head_splits[p]` 表示「rank p 拥有的序列片长 / 头片数」，这是**组几何**的描述，与数据向哪个方向流动无关（这个性质在 u6-l3 讲 backward 时会再次出现：backward 不交换 splits）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

记 \( s_{\text{global}} = \sum_p \text{seq\_splits}[p] \)，\( n_{\text{global}} = \sum_p \text{head\_splits}[p] \)，\( n_{\text{local}} = \text{head\_splits}[\text{rank}] \)，\( s_{\text{local}} = \text{seq\_splits}[\text{rank}] \)。

不传 splits 时，由形状反推偶均分：

- mode 0 输入 `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` → 推得 `seq_splits = [s_local]*ws`、`head_splits = [n_global/ws]*ws`
- mode 1 输入 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` → 推得 `seq_splits = [s_global/ws]*ws`、`head_splits = [n_local]*ws`

然后套用形状表：

| mode | 输入 | 输出 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 — 散头、聚序列 | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` |
| 1 — 逆变换 | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` |

推导顺序（伪代码）：

```text
resolve_splits(x_shape, mode, ws, splits?):
    if splits 缺失:
        mode 0: 要求 n_global % ws == 0；seq=[x1]*ws, head=[x2/ws]*ws
        mode 1: 要求 s_global % ws == 0；seq=[x1/ws]*ws, head=[x2]*ws
    else:
        两组都必须给，且与 x 的形状交叉吻合
    if mode == 0: return (b, sum(seq), head[rank], d)
    else:         return (b, seq[rank],  sum(head), d)
```

注意 `ws = 1` 的特例：`s_local == s_global`、`n_local == n_global`，两个 mode 的形状都退化成恒等——这就是为什么 u1-l3 说「world_size=1 是合法一等公民」，可以用它做单卡冒烟测试。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

真正的形状推导在 `src/group.cc` 的 `make_dims`。先看偶均分特例——mode 0 检查被散射的轴（头轴）能整除，然后直接从形状造出两组 splits：

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`ws=8`，输入 `(1, 4096, 40, 384)`，`mode=0`，不传 splits。会发生什么？

**答案**：mode 0 要求头轴整除：`n_global=40`，`40 % 8 == 0`，合法。推得 `seq_splits=[4096]*8`、`head_splits=[5]*8`，输出 `(1, 32768, 5, 384)`。若头数换成 44（`44 % 8 != 0`），则在 `make_dims` 抛 `RuntimeError`，消息以 `mode 0 scatters the head axis` 开头。

**练习 2**：mode 1 下输入 `(2, 128, 6, 64)`、`ws=4`、不传 splits，输出是什么？反过来把输出喂给 mode 0 会得到什么？

**答案**：mode 1 输入形状是 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)`，检查 `128 % 4 == 0`，推得 `seq_splits=[32]*4`、`head_splits=[6]*4`，输出 `(2, 32, 24, 64)`。把 `(2, 32, 24, 64)` 喂给 mode 0：检查 `24 % 4 == 0`，`seq_splits=[32]*4`、`head_splits=[6]*4`，输出 `(2, 128, 6, 64)`——还原成最初输入。两次调用互逆，这正是 u2-l4 示例里「包夹注意力」成立的前提。

**练习 3**：为什么 `ws=1` 时任何头数都不会触发整除检查的报错？

**答案**：任何整数对 1 取模都是 0。`make_dims` 的两个整除分支（`x2 % ws`、`x1 % ws`）在 `ws=1` 下恒真，所以该检查在单 rank 下「不可达」——这也是本讲综合实践中我们无法在 `ws=1` 下测整除报错的原因（test/distributed/validation.py:L123 对此有同样的备注）。

### 4.2 dtype 白名单与 16 字节对齐

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

传输层搬运的是**字节**，不理解数值含义——`build_plan` 只接收一个 `elem_size`，窗口和 plan 缓存的键里带 dtype，仅此而已。既然如此，为什么要限制 dtype？

因为「接受哪些类型」是一个**产品决策而非技术约束**：源码注释明确说这是「listed, not opened up」（列出来的，不是推导出来的）。放行 `kBool`、复数、量化类型意味着要为这些没人推理过的类型背书。于是白名单收下训练里实际会用的 7 种：`float16 / bfloat16 / float32 / float8_e4m3fn / float8_e5m2 / int8 / uint8`。

对齐规则 `d * elem_size` 必须是 16 的倍数，来自传输的物理形态：拷贝引擎按「一行 `d * elem_size` 字节」做二维/三维拷贝（u3、u5 展开），所有偏移、步长、宽度都是这个数的倍数。**检查一行，对齐全局**——这是把一条约束放在最便宜位置（纯主机、进 plan 缓存键）的典型设计。

注意规则的**不对称收紧**：约束的是字节数不是维数，所以元素越窄，对 `d` 的要求越苛刻。fp16 要 `d % 8 == 0`，fp32 只需 `d % 4 == 0`，fp8/int8 则要 `d % 16 == 0`。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

被接受的 dtype 与对应的对齐要求：

| dtype | elem_size | 对 `d` 的要求 | 例：`d=128` | 例：`d=8` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| float16 | 2 B | \( d \times 2 \equiv 0 \pmod{16} \Rightarrow d \bmod 8 = 0 \) | ✅ 256 B | ✅ 16 B |
| bfloat16 | 2 B | `d % 8 == 0` | ✅ | ✅ |
| float32 | 4 B | `d % 4 == 0` | ✅ | ✅ |
| float8_e4m3fn / float8_e5m2 | 1 B | `d % 16 == 0` | ✅ | ❌ 8 B |
| int8 / uint8 | 1 B | `d % 16 == 0` | ✅ | ❌ 8 B |

检查流程（`make_dims` 内，进入 splits 逻辑之前）：

```text
取 d = sizes[3]，elem = elementSize(dtype)
检查 (d * elem) % 16 == 0
    失败 → "the head dim must be 16-byte aligned: d=.. x .. B is .. B"
```

一个直接推论：`d=8` 在 bfloat16 下合法、转成 float8_e4m3fn 后非法——同一个形状在不同 dtype 下对齐结论不同，test/distributed/validation.py:L103-L108 专门测了这一条。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

dtype 白名单与「这是决策不是约束」的注释：

[src/group.cc:L59-L62](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L59-L62)

```cpp
                || dtype == at::kFloat8_e5m2 || dtype == at::kChar || dtype == at::kByte,
```
